Australia's agriculture sector is an important contributor to the national economy and employs millions of people across the country. With a very diverse climate, the majority of agricultural production is concentrated in the southeastern part of Australia and mostly within a narrow strip less than 100 km wide from Sydney to Melbourne. The south-eastern part of Australia is mainly mountainous region, and a certain level of topographic variability can influence the land surface conditions. The rugged and complex topography of this region makes it challenging for the remote sensing practitioners to produce accurate maps. The Landsat satellites have been providing valuable data for mapping and monitoring cropland extent for decades. In 1972, the very first Landsat satellite was launched by NASA and USGS, which provided various multispectral data. The spectral resolution of the Landsat data was coarse, and thus it may not be appropriate for mapping small cropland parcels. From 2013 onwards, Landsat-8 has been collecting optical data in 11 spectral bands with two new spectral bands in shortwave infrared (SWIR) region. The spectral resolution of the Landsat-8 data is better, and thus it is expected to be more suitable for high-resolution cropland mapping. The authors developed a supervised machine learning model using the random forest classifier to classify cropland from other land cover types. The Landsat-8 images were collected over the study areas on two random dates selected from 2015. The study regions were divided into randomly assigned training and test areas with the training set used for model development. They collected ground truth data for cropland and other land cover types in their training areas using Google Earth. The developed model was tested on the test areas and showed an overall accuracy of 94% for Australia and 95% for China. The model was able to correctly identify the cropland pixels with an overall producer's accuracy (PA) of 95% and user's accuracy (UA) of 95%. The methodology works well for topographically rugged areas, and thus a large extent of cropland across the entire Australia can be modeled. "High-resolution land cover information is crucial for understanding crop growth and productivity as well as for monitoring land use, land cover change, and environmental impacts," said Krishna.

The aim is to create a friendly environment where children can learn and grow in all aspects. Children's community resource centers will offer a safe haven for children where they can engage in educational, recreational and skill development activities. It will be a center that welcomes children from their own communities regardless of their economic backgrounds. These centers will promote a sense of belonging, inclusion and mutual learning among children. Community resource centers for children in Uganda are spaces that provide children with the opportunity to develop their skills and abilities. These centers are often run by organizations working to improve the lives of children in low-income communities and serve as a hub for various activities. The aim is to provide children with a safe and nurturing environment where they can learn, play and grow. The community resource center for children in Uganda will provide a range of educational, recreational and skill development activities. They will be open to children from their own communities regardless of their economic backgrounds and will promote a sense of belonging, inclusion and mutual learning. There are several potential benefits of establishing these types of centers in Uganda. For children, they will provide access to quality education and extracurricular activities that may not be available in their own homes. The children will also have the opportunity to develop important social skills, teamwork and leadership abilities through group activities. Moreover, community resource centers can provide a safe space for children to spend their free time away from potentially unsafe environments. For parents, community resource centers can provide a respite from their daily struggles and responsibilities. Parents may feel more supported in raising their children and have access to resources and guidance that they may not have otherwise. Additionally, it can provide a social network for parents to connect with other parents in their community and share experiences and advice. For the communities, community resource centers can have a positive impact on the overall well-being of children. It can provide a sense of security and stability for families who may be experiencing financial or social challenges.
